sections.text: Many have merged their existences in Mine, being freed from desire, fear and anger, filled always with Me and purified by the illuminating flame of self-abnegation.
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम्।
Howsoever men try to worship Me, so do I welcome them. By whatever path they travel, it leads to Me at last.
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः।
Those who look for success, worship the Powers; and in this world their actions bear immediate fruit.

Chapter 4 Gnana Karma Sannyasi Yoga of Ending Karma in Knowledge. We all want to retire, but there is no real practical way to retire. You always do something.
You can only retire mentally. So when you dont take your actions to be work, you retire, then you enjoy this. So when we change our mental attitude about our actions, then you retire from the actions.
So the only way Bhagavan says to end your actions because these actions are binding and I want to get out of this bondage. He said, you have to get rid of your actions. You have to retire from your actions.
And the only way to retire is in the knowledge of who you are and what actions are all about. So in chapter three we have seen Karma Yoga and see how to gradually liberate yourself from your actions by changing your attitude towards actions. And now you say, well, how can I then completely relieve myself of this burden is to realize who I am.
So this chapter talks about what is the nature of the self. Ajaha Pisan Avya Yatman. I yourself, Ajaha Unborn, Avyatma, immutable, imperishable.
Thats the real nature of mind. Bhutanam Isvaropisan. I am the lord of all beings.
All beings are beings because of my presence in them. I am who I am and you are who you are. And the donkey is who donkey is.
Because that life which is pulsating through them, the presence of that omnipresent self makes people who they are and beings who they are. Thats why he is the lord of all the beings. Lordship is someone who has a control over my life is my lord in feudal system.
The guy who owned the estate was a lord. Even today hes a landlord and a renter. He has the control over your property.
Therefore hes a landlord. So he is the Bhutana Mishurabeesan. Prakrutin swam this tyre.
You and I come into existence because of the Self. But because of the Maya we think we are individual egos, we are the individuals. But someone who has a complete identification with himself, he realizes this is just an appearance.
Its just an illusion that I have taken a limited form. So the difference between us and the Avatar is we think we are limited. Avatar knows all the time.
His role in this life is limited. So Krishna can say, I am unlimited. He knew his role in this life, but he never bound himself with his role.
He said that presiding over my prakriti, I come time and again to regulate Dharma. Hi Dharma Siglanir Bhavati. Dharma itself is a self regulating principle. You dont really need to do anything about Dharma water.
You dont have to train water to seek its own level because its self regulating. My Dharma is also self regulating. So when I get out of my Dharma, I cease to be what I was.
Ill become something else. When I came to this country, there were no jobs for architecture because I came in 82 and there was a recess in time. So there were no jobs.
So people said, Rajan, the best thing you can do. And I was in Houston at the time, so the oil economy was still tail end of it. The best thing, if you can become a pipe designer, pipe drafting, pipe drafting.
Pipe drafting is a lot of money. So compared to architecture, you do pipe drafting, all those pipes for the oil company, you will make more money. And I said, no matter how much money there is, I wont be able to do it.
Thats my Dharma to design building. I cant design pipes. I may have to suffer through unemployment.
As long as I dont get a job, Ill do something else. But by very nature, Im an architect. I have to design buildings.
And then I finally somewhere I worked for some contractor. I think you will do very well if you continue in the contracting. I left the job right away.
He is going to deviate me from my Dharma. So what is your Dharma if I stop being an architect or stop designing buildings? Im not an architect. Its as simple as that.
So Dharma is a self regulating principle. To remain who I am, I have to remain in that Dharma. As soon as I deviate from that Dharma, Dharma itself, eliminate me from that existence, stop practicing architecture, Ill be eliminated from architectural societies, architectural communities, all the architectural duties and responsibilities.
Im not something else. So Bhagwan says, yada yada, Hi Dharma Seglani R. Bhavati.
In this world, a role is assigned to each thing and being. If they deviate from the Dharma, I will eliminate them. As the regulating principle, to be the agency that does this, I will take Avatara.
I will be a catalyst to make the change for those who are deviating from the Dharma. To eliminate from that society, that community, that part of this universe. Abyutthanam, adharmasyatadhatmanam sujam.
When there is a rise of Adharma, a lot of people are thinking that this is Dharma, but actually its Adharma. So when that happens, when Dharma is misunderstood by beings and people, as the last time we have discussed, its only for human beings because we have free will that we can deviate from our Dharma. We can be vegetarians and also can be non vegetarians.
We dont know whether we were designed as vegetarians or not. Elephant knows he is designed as vegetarian. Lion knows he is designed as carnivore.
Because of our free will, we deviate from our Dharma when it becomes unbearable for the society. You also, you know, surjami aham. During springtime, you see, when there are few weeds in your garden, you see, its okay.
You dont pay much attention to it. Then gradually your yard becomes filled with weeds. Then less grass and more weeds.
Then one Sunday, you put on your yard work clothes and say, I need to take care of this. You will tolerate it to a point. Let the weeds have good time.
And then one Sunday you say, no, this is it or the protection of the grass. Vina Sahaja duskritam all the way. So time and again you, as the Lord will come and set your yard right.
Bhagawan said this, in my yard, I have to do the same thing. Paritra Naya Sadhunam Vinasaya. Somebody asked a teacher.
They say, but if thats the case, why Bhagavan is not coming now? He said, Bhagavan clearly says Paritra Naya, Sadhuna. If lesser evil is fighting with greater evil, Bhagavan has nothing to do with it. Let them figure it out how to kill each other.
They will eliminate each other automatically. Bhagavan doesnt have to interfere. It is only that evil is not letting the good practice good.
Then only Bhagavan comes. In our case, its a lesser evil fighting greater evil. Its still evil in the end.
Therefore, he said, Bhagavan doesnt have to come yet. Dharma Sasthapanaarthaya. To establish Dharma again. As I said, its a self regulating principle.
It will time and again it will reset Dharma so that the cycle will continue as it was designed. We take our car once in a while for tune up and wheel alignment. We tolerate it to a point.
When it starts making noise while youre driving, I need to take it to the garage and calibrate it. So that is a self regulating principle to calibrate itself. Because time and again it gets out of its alignment.
And Bhagawan said, I as the self. I created this universe out of my own self, out of my own Maya. And I let it run through its own laws.
The laws of nature are self regulating. So we dont have to control whatever the law of gravity and all that. We dont want to get up in the morning.
Lets make sure the law of gravity is working. Otherwise how Im going to go down to the staircase. Because suddenly if I try to go down, I start flying into the ceiling.
So I have to be very conscious that law of gravity is working every day. No, we dont have to. But my own behavior I have to regulate.
Because I have free will. I can be doing right. I also can be doing wrong.
My free will is guided my mind and intellect and my mind and intellect can deceive me in doing something which is not right. I say I should not be doing this. But the mind will put an argument and say no.
Other people are doing it. So whats wrong in it then? Everybodys doing it. Cheating on 1040 because other people are doing it.
I come to think that its okay. But my conscience tell me its not right. But my mind and intellect will say thats okay.
And thats what I suffer. So Bhagawan says, thats why I have to time and again rise in your own heart as your own inner voice. If I have few good thoughts which are still trying to direct me toward the right path, but many bad thoughts are avoiding me to exercise my right to follow the good thoughts, then that voice will rise in my heart.
Because at least those good thoughts were propelling me to find what is right. So thats what Bhagawan said. I will rise in your heart as your avatar.
And that will redeem you from the Wrong that you are going to do, when will that happen? Janma Karma Chame Divyam evam yo Vidya Takvatah -- when you will realize that in its essence, I am the divine being, that this life is divine, given to me for learning to rise out of limitations. Once I realize what is the real truth, what is my real nature, then when I get out of this existence, when I exhaust all the vasanas and karmas of this existence, I will not take a new birth. If last time I experienced something and that was not really enjoyable, I somehow suffered through that experience.
But then what will I do next? I dont want to go there again ever. Because I realized that this is a painful existence. It is when we go back and forth I enjoyed some but suffer some.
So let me go for the enjoyment in the bargain I also suffer. So thats why we have Punarabi Janamam Punarapi Maranam because our attachments are taking us back to that existence Even though we suffered through it we forget at times that there will be sufferings also attached to this pleasures. But once I realize my divine nature is omnipresence and omnipotence, I will get out of this Punarjanma.
So Tektvadeham Punarjunmati Saharjuna -- he comes to being my own self. The technique is now given, and we have discussed before that the root cause is attachment, and its byproducts are Raga, Bhaya and Krodha. Raga (attachment) is the root cause; Bhaya (fear) and Krodha (anger) are the byproducts.
Once I realize thats the root cause, if I start getting out of attachment, fear and anger will not be there. He said therefore the goal is to get rid of attachment. But I cant get rid of attachment unless I take refuge in something higher.
Maam Upa Sri Tah -- one who takes refuge in me. Then that me is the I that I keep reciting all my life. If I take refuge in my I and do not rely on my body, mind and intellect to give me the peace and happiness which I am seeking, then I will be liberated. Liberated from attachment.
Once I am liberated from attachment, I will be liberated from fear and anger. Bahavogna Tapasa Puta Madbhavam Agatha -- again we have to be reminded: you are not the guinea pig.

These verses reveal the path to liberation through the purification of attachment, fear, and anger (vita-raga-bhaya-krodha). Many have attained the divine state by taking refuge in the Lord and becoming purified by the fire of knowledge (jnana-tapasa puta). The root cause is attachment (raga), with fear and anger being its byproducts. Krishna teaches that by releasing attachment and taking refuge in the higher Self (mam upashritah), one becomes free from these binding emotions.
The beautiful verse ye yatha mam prapadyante tams tathaiva bhajamy aham reveals the universal nature of grace: however people approach the Divine, in that very manner does the Divine respond. All paths ultimately lead to the same destination. However, those seeking quick, measurable results in this world worship various powers and deities, because worldly success is easily visible and attainable. The challenge is that attachment to these results creates further bondage.
For daily practice, identify the primary attachments driving your actions today. Are you pursuing something because of genuine dharma or because you seek quick, visible results? Notice when fear or anger arise - trace them back to the underlying attachment. Practice the teaching mam upashritah - taking refuge in your own higher Self rather than in external outcomes. Ask yourself: Can I remain in my authentic nature (like an architect who refuses to design pipes because it is not his dharma) even when external pressures push me otherwise? When you find yourself attached to outcomes, remind yourself that the Self within is actionless, unborn, and Lord of all beings (bhutanam ishvaropi san).
